newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end lower, widen losses late.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end lower, widen losses late.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed lower after key currencies expanded losses late in the day on comments from U.S. administration officials ahead of the G7 meeting on Sunday, traders said.
June yen set daily lows in the last 20 minutes of trade after President Clinton said he and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto agreed on the need for strong demand-led growth in Japan.
June yen eased to $0.007972 in extremely light trade.
Clinton and Hashimoto also agreed at their morning meeting to intensify Japanese deregulation talks.

The comments, which followed U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin's statements at a press briefing, suggested that the G7 nation's dollar policy would not be changed to accommodate Japan's recovery, traders and analysts said.
June marks fell to $0.5803, below the contract low settlement of $0.5809, after Rubin repeated that the dollar policy was unchanged. June Swiss francs fell to a fresh one-week low at $0.6837.
However, a few traders said sentiment that dollar policy would stay the same was slightly undercut by Rubin's remark that he shared Japan's concern about the weakness in the yen.
"He (Rubin) seems to be taking lessons from Alan Greenspan," one foreign currency trader said.
"He says that the dollar has been strong, and that fundamentals are supporting the dollar, but then says he shares Japan's concerns about the yen," he said.
Several traders said Rubin's comments left open the possibility the G7 nations might formulate a forex policy that includes dollar intervention.
"It is certainly a concern," another currency trader said.
However, he said many U.S. investors had already trimmed long dollar positions against the yen in anticipation that the G7 nations would change dollar policy.
"I think there has been a lot of lightening of positions ahead of Sunday's meeting, he said.

One technical analyst said June marks appeared to be forming a base, but would have to close above $0.6055, the 2-1/2-month high set on March 31, to turn the trend higher. Likewise, June Swiss francs would have to close above above $0.7063, the 2-1/4-month high hit on April 3, and June yen would have to close above $0.008335 to change the downtrend.

At the end of pit trade, June yen was down $0.000014 at $0.007976, marks down $0.0043 at $0.5812, Swiss francs off $0.0042 at $0.6844, sterling down $0.0028 at $1.6218, Can dollars off $0.0018 at $0.7184 and Aussie dollars up $0.0007 at $0.7768.
